title: Combustion of octane with 400 % theoretical air
summary: Octane burned with 400 % theoretical air in steady flow: adiabatic flame temperature from the first law on the combustion reaction (formation enthalpies), fuel-air ratio and stoichiometric dosage; excess-air effect on the flame temperature.
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée MECA0002 repetition team)

name: diesel_engine_excess_air_exhaust_analysis
title: Diesel engine: excess air and useful power from exhaust-gas analysis
summary: Combustion of diesel fuel (CH_n, n fitted from C/H mass fractions) with excess air; the excess air follows from the fuel-air ratio and the useful power from the five-box energy balance of the course, with the products brought to the exhaust temperature of 432 °C.
tags: combustion;diesel engine;exhaust gas analysis;excess air;fuel-air ratio;exercise
authors: TBD (ULiège, MECA0002 Thermodynamique appliquée, course of S. Quoilin)

name: steam_turbine_exergy_balance
title: Steam turbine exergy balance
summary: Second-law (exergy) analysis of a steam turbine of a ULiège course exercise: steam enters at 3 MPa and 450 °C at 8 kg/s, leaves at 0.2 MPa and 150 °C and loses 300 kW to an ambient at 100 kPa and 25 °C; the model gives the actual and the maximum (reversible) power, the second-law efficiency, the exergy destruction and the specific flow exergy at the inlet.
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002)

name: two_tanks_connected_valve_r12
title: Two rigid tanks connected by a valve: change of quality of R12
summary: Two rigid tanks of 200 L connected by a valve: tank A holds an R12 liquid-vapour mixture at 25 C (10 % liquid and 90 % vapour in volume) and tank B is empty; opening the valve lets saturated vapour into B at constant temperature until the pressures are equal. The model gives the initial and the final quality of tank A (change of +6.67 percentage points) and the liquid/vapour distribution of the whole volume.
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002)

name: iron_block_quench_water_tank
title: Iron block quenched in a water tank (exergy destruction)
summary: Closed-system second-law exercise: a 5 kg iron block at 350 degC quenched in 100 kg of water at 30 degC in an insulated rigid tank; the first law gives the final equilibrium temperature and the exergy balance of the isolated system gives the exergy destruction (wasted work potential).
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée; the companion course files name S. Quoilin and the repetition assistants N. Paulus and B. Dechesne)

name: two_tanks_max_work_air
title: Maximum work from two air tanks at 900 K and 300 K
summary: Two rigid vessels of 30 kg of air at 900 K and 300 K are coupled by a heat engine; the reversible (maximum work) end state is computed from the entropy balance of the extended system: both vessels end at the geometric mean temperature 519.6 K and the engine delivers 3.60 MJ.
tags: exergy;maximum work;reversible process;rigid tank;ideal gas;entropy balance;heat engine;exercise
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002)

name: methane_tank_evaporation
title: Evaporation of liquid methane in a tank
summary: Liquid methane at 500 kPa in a tank evaporates due to heat input (level drop of 30 mm per hour); the model computes the evaporated mass and the volumetric flow rate of the gas leaving a heater at 500 kPa and 275 K.
authors: TBD

name: rigid_tank_water_mixture
title: Rigid tank with a liquid-vapour water mixture
summary: A 1 m^3 rigid vessel contains 4 kg of water in liquid-vapour equilibrium at 6 bar: quality of the mixture from the average specific volume, masses and volumes of the liquid and vapour phases, saturation temperature.
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée MECA0002 repetition team)

name: nonideal_gas_isothermal_work
title: Isothermal expansion of a non-ideal gas: unit of k and boundary work
summary: A gas obeying the equation of state v*(P + k/v^2) = R*T expands isothermally from 2 m^3 to 4 m^3; the model gives the unit of the parameter k, the final pressure and the boundary work, computed with an EES definite integral and with the closed form (the two must agree).
tags: equation of state;non-ideal gas;boundary work;isothermal;definite integral;dimensional analysis;exercise
authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée MECA0002 repetition team)

name: pipe_pressure_drop_colebrook
title: Pipe pressure drop with the Colebrook-White friction factor
summary: Friction pressure drop of n-pentane in a straight pipe (16 mm diameter, 10 m): Darcy friction factor from the implicit Colebrook-White equation checked against an explicit approximation, linear and total pressure drop, dynamic pressure.
authors: Vincent Lemort (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory); S. Quoilin (CoolSolve example)

name: chilled_water_cooling_coil
title: Chilled-water air cooling coil, dry and wet regimes
summary: Chilled-water air cooling coil (series air/wall/water resistances): dry regime by counterflow epsilon-NTU, condensation-risk check, wet regime by wet-bulb effectiveness with contact-factor outlet state and condensate flow.
authors: Stéphane Bertagnolio (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory); S. Quoilin (CoolSolve example)

name: air_handling_unit_moist_air
title: Air handling unit with moist-air conditioning
summary: Room supplied with outdoor air through an air handling unit: supply state from the room sensible and moisture loads, cooling coil by contact effectiveness with post-heating; computes coil capacity, post-heating power and condensate flow.
authors: Vincent Lemort (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory); S. Quoilin (CoolSolve example)

name: cooling_coil_condensate_ratio
title: Condensate ratio and dry-air flow at a cooling coil, and a counter-flow recuperator
summary: Revision exercise with two questions on one heat-pump cycle: (1) a 7 kW cooling coil that dehumidifies air from 28 C/80 % RH to 13 C saturated, solved with two first-law methods (humid-air enthalpies neglecting the condensate, or separate dry-air/vapour/condensate terms), giving the condensate-to-dry-air ratio and the dry-air flow; (2) a counter-flow R113 recuperator of effectiveness 60 % with 5 kPa pressure drops on both sides, giving the outlet temperature T10.
authors: TBD (ULiège course MECA0002; inventory suggests S. Quoilin with repetition assistants N. Paulus and B. Dechesne)

name: adiabatic_humidifier_simplified
title: Adiabatic humidifier, simplified model (effectiveness-NTU)
summary: Adiabatic (evaporative) humidifier on humid air: heat and moisture transfer effectiveness from an NTU whose conductance follows power laws in the air and water flow rates (laboratory identification); exit air state and fraction of the supplied water evaporated.
authors: Jean Lebrun (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory)

name: two_speed_cooling_tower
title: Two-speed cooling tower (regimes and mean fan power vs water set-point)
summary: Evaporative cooling tower with a two-speed fan, each regime rated with the epsilon-NTU method on a fictitious dry fluid following the wet-bulb temperatures of the moist air; returns the outlet temperatures, heat rejected and weighted-mean fan powers for a given water outlet set-point.
authors: ULiège MSTh course (J. Lebrun, V. Lemort, S. Bertagnolio); S. Quoilin (CoolSolve example)

name: cooling_tower_condenser_water
title: Cooling tower for the condenser water of a steam power plant
summary: Level-1 mass (dry air, water) and energy balances of a direct-contact cooling tower cooling condenser water from 65 °C to 30 °C with ambient air: air volume flow rate, make-up water flow rate and condenser heat rate.
authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, S. Quoilin; repetition assistants N. Paulus and B. Dechesne per companion metadata)

name: moist_air_cooling_coil_contact_factor
title: Moist-air cooling coil with contact factor
summary: Moist air cooled over a coil of given mean surface temperature: contact factor applied to temperatures and humidity ratios, total/sensible/latent heat per kg of dry air and condensate mass.
authors: Vincent Lemort (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory); S. Quoilin (CoolSolve example)

name: moist_air_room_psychrometrics
title: Moist air in a room: humidity ratio, enthalpy and dew point
summary: Room of 5 m x 5 m x 3 m filled with air at 25 C and 75 % relative humidity at 100 kPa: partial pressures, humidity ratio, specific enthalpy per kg of dry air, masses of dry air and of water vapour, and dew-point temperature of the room air; every quantity is computed both with the course relations and with the EES property functions.
authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002 - see README 'Source and attribution')

name: moist_air_adiabatic_mixing
title: Adiabatic mixing of room air and outdoor air (moist air)
summary: Room air (dry-bulb/wet-bulb given) mixed adiabatically with outdoor air (temperature and relative humidity given): dry-air and vapour mass balances and a first-law balance give the humidity ratio and specific enthalpy of the supply state, plus its temperature, dew point and relative humidity.
authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002 - see README 'Source and attribution')

name: psychrometric_mixer_condensation
title: Psychrometric mixer with condensation: room air mixed with outdoor air
summary: Room air (20 degC dry bulb, 19.2 degC wet bulb) mixed adiabatically with outdoor air (0 degC, 90 % relative humidity, 300 g/s of dry air) at 101 325 Pa; the mixture falls below saturation, so the balances of the dry air, of the water (with a condensate term) and of the energy give the temperature of the saturated mixture and the condensate flow rate.
authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002 - see README 'Source and attribution')

name: adiabatic_saturation_wet_bulb
title: Adiabatic saturation and wet-bulb temperature of moist air
summary: Air at 25 degC dry bulb and 15 degC wet bulb at 1 atm: specific humidity, relative humidity and specific enthalpy of the moist air per kg of dry air, obtained with the adiabatic-saturation formula of the course (mass and energy balances of a wet-bulb thermometer, constant heat capacities) and cross-checked with the EES property functions HumRat, RelHum and enthalpy.
authors: TBD (ULiège course Thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002 - see README 'Source and attribution')
